+  },
+
+  onShow() {
+    this.reload()
+  },
+
+  async reload() {
+    if (this.data.loadingSales) return
+    this.setData({ loadingSales: true })
+    const finishInitial = () => {
+      if (this.data.initialLoading || !this.data.initialLoaded) {
+        this.setData({ initialLoading: false, initialLoaded: true })
+      }
+    }
+    try {
+      const salesRes = await call('admin', 'listFulfillmentSales', { limit: 50, includeCompleted: true })
+      if (!salesRes.ok) {
+        finishInitial()
+        this.setData({
+          saleOptions: [{ label: '加载失败', value: '', status: '' }],
+          saleIndex: 0,
+          saleLabel: '加载失败',
+          sale: null,
+          canOperate: false,
+          orders: [],
+          appendedHint: '',
+        })
+        wx.showToast({ title: salesRes.message || '加载失败', icon: 'none' })
+        return
+      }
+      const sales = Array.isArray(salesRes.data && salesRes.data.sales) ? salesRes.data.sales : []
+      const opts = sales.map((s) => ({
+        label: buildSaleLabel(s),
+        value: String(s._id || ''),
+        status: String(s.status || ''),
+      }))
+      if (!opts.length) opts.push({ label: '暂无可交付开单', value: '', status: '' })
+      const currentValue = (this.data.saleOptions[this.data.saleIndex] && this.data.saleOptions[this.data.saleIndex].value) || ''
+      const saleIndex = pickSaleIndex(opts, this.prefSaleId, currentValue)
+      const picked = opts[saleIndex] || { label: '未选择', value: '' }
+      this.setData({
+        saleOptions: opts,
+        saleIndex,
+        saleLabel: picked.label || '未选择',
+      })
+      finishInitial()
+      await this.loadRun()
+    } finally {
+      this.setData({ loadingSales: false })
+    }
+  },
+
+  onPickSale(e) {
+    const saleIndex = Number((e.detail && e.detail.value) || 0)
+    const picked = this.data.saleOptions[saleIndex] || { label: '未选择', value: '' }
+    this.setData({
+      saleIndex,
+      saleLabel: picked.label || '未选择',
+      appendedHint: '',
+    })
+    this.loadRun()
+  },
+
+  async loadRun() {
+    const option = this.data.saleOptions[this.data.saleIndex] || null

+      if (this.data.initialLoading || !this.data.initialLoaded) {
+        this.setData({ initialLoading: false, initialLoaded: true })
+      }
+    }
+    if (!saleId) {
+      this.setData({
+        sale: null,
+        canOperate: false,
+        orders: [],
+        appendedHint: '',
+        summary: { totalActiveOrders: 0, deliveredOrders: 0, paidOrders: 0, doneOrders: 0, remainingOrders: 0 },

+      return

+    finishInitial()

+        sale: null,
+        canOperate: false,

+        appendedHint: '',

+    const appendedOrderIds =
+      (res.data && res.data.derived && Array.isArray(res.data.derived.appendedOrderIds) && res.data.derived.appendedOrderIds) || []
+    this.setData({
+      sale: (res.data && res.data.sale) || null,
+      canOperate: !!(res.data && res.data.canOperate),
+      summary:
+        (res.data && res.data.summary) ||
+        { totalActiveOrders: 0, deliveredOrders: 0, paidOrders: 0, doneOrders: 0, remainingOrders: 0 },
+      orders: rawOrders.map(decorateRunOrder),

+  },
+
+  onOrderAction(e) {

+    if (!Number.isFinite(idx) || idx < 0 || idx >= this.data.orders.length) return
+    const order = this.data.orders[idx]
+    if (!order || !order._id) return
+    wx.showActionSheet({
+      itemList: ACTIONS.map((x) => x.label),
+      success: async (res) => {
+        const action = ACTIONS[Number(res.tapIndex)]
+        if (!action) return
+        if (action.key === 'view_detail') {
+          wx.navigateTo({ url: `/pages/admin/order-detail/index?orderId=${encodeURIComponent(order._id)}` })
+          return
+        }
+        if (action.key === 'set_cash') {
+          await this.applyOrderProgress(order._id, { paymentMethod: 'cash' }, '已切换为现金')
+          return
+        }
+        if (action.key === 'set_transfer') {
+          await this.applyOrderProgress(order._id, { paymentMethod: 'wechat_transfer' }, '已切换为转账')
+          return
+        }
+        if (action.key === 'mark_delivered') {
+          await this.applyOrderProgress(order._id, { handoffStatus: 'DELIVERED' }, '已标记送达')
+          return
+        }
+        if (action.key === 'mark_paid') {
+          await this.applyOrderProgress(order._id, { paidStatus: 'PAID' }, '已标记收款')
+          return
+        }
+        if (action.key === 'mark_paid_and_delivered') {
+          await this.applyOrderProgress(order._id, { paidStatus: 'PAID', handoffStatus: 'DELIVERED' }, '已标记完成')
+        }
+      },
+    })
+  },
+
+  async applyOrderProgress(orderId, patch, successTitle) {
+    if (this.data.operatingOrderId) return
+    const saleId = String((this.data.sale && this.data.sale._id) || '').trim()
+    this.setData({ operatingOrderId: orderId })
+    const res = await call('admin', 'updateOrderFulfillmentProgress', {
+      orderId,
+      saleId,
+      ...patch,
+    })
+    this.setData({ operatingOrderId: '' })
+    if (!res.ok) {
+      wx.showToast({ title: res.message || '更新失败', icon: 'none' })
+      await this.loadRun()
+      return
+    }
+    wx.showToast({ title: successTitle || '已更新', icon: 'success' })
+    await this.loadRun()
+  },
+
+  async onCompleteSale() {
+    if (!this.data.canOperate || this.data.completingSale || !this.data.sale || !this.data.sale._id) return

+      wx.showModal({
+        title: '标记开单完成',
+        content: '仅当所有有效订单都已交付且已收款时才能完成。',
+        success: resolve,
+        fail: () => resolve({ confirm: false }),
+      })
+    })
+    if (!modalRes.confirm) return
+    this.setData({ completingSale: true })
+    const res = await call('admin', 'completeSaleFulfillment', { saleId: this.data.sale._id })
+    this.setData({ completingSale: false })
+    if (!res.ok) {

+      if (res.code === 'SALE_NOT_READY_TO_COMPLETE') {
+        const undelivered = Number(detail.undeliveredCount || 0)
+        const unpaid = Number(detail.unpaidCount || 0)

+      } else {
+        wx.showToast({ title: res.message || '完成失败', icon: 'none' })
+      }
+      await this.loadRun()
+      return
+    }
+    wx.showToast({ title: '开单已完成', icon: 'success' })
+    await this.reload()
+  },
+})
+
*** End Patch

**本次实现内容**
- 新增店主端页面
  - `pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index`（交付准备：手动排序，先做上移/下移）
  - `pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index`（交付执行：按排序处理交付/收款）

  - `交付准备`

  - `saleFulfillmentPlans`

- `listFulfillmentSales`
- `getSaleFulfillmentPrep`
- `saveSaleFulfillmentOrder`
- `getSaleFulfillmentRun`

会有影响，但取决于你部署了什么、改动是否兼容。

你这个项目当前情况（这次改了 `admin` / `customer` 云函数）：

- 对**店主端**：会立刻生效（因为云函数是服务端，部署后新请求都走新代码）
- 对**客人端**：如果调用到你改过的 `customer` 行为，也会立刻生效
- 对已经发布的小程序客户端：**不需要用户更新小程序版本，也会吃到新云函数逻辑**

关键点是“兼容性”：
- 如果新云函数**改了返回结构/行为**，而旧前端还在调用旧逻辑，可能出问题
- 如果只是新增 action、兼容式扩展字段，一般影响小

你这次这批改动里：
- `admin` 新增了很多 action（给新页面用）→ 对旧已发布客人端基本没影响
- `customer` 增加了订单写入 `handoffStatus` 字段 → 通常兼容，不会影响旧前端
- 但是你如果**已发布版本里店主页调用的 `admin.getDashboard` / 其他 action 依赖旧行为**，就要谨慎（目前看这次没破坏性改老 action 的主返回字段，风险较低）

**结论（实操建议）**
1. 如果你现在线上还有人在用，先在测试环境/测试云环境部署（最稳）
2. 如果就是你自己在测试，可以直接部署
3. 部署前后重点回归：
   - 客人下单
   - 店主开单/截单
   - 订单管理/订单详情
   - 新增交付准备/交付执行

另外一个实际影响：
- 你这次新增了集合 `saleFulfillmentPlans`
- 如果没建集合就进“交付准备”点保存，会报错（我已经加了提示）

如果你愿意，我可以下一步给你一份“**这次部署的最小回归清单（5分钟版）**”，你照着点一遍就知道有没有影响。

<collaboration_mode># Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

item.text:
## 重构 Sale 生命周期状态（从“开单/截单”扩展到“配送中/完成”的显式状态）

### Summary
你这个判断是对的。现在 `sale` 状态虽然技术上已有 `DRAFT / OPEN / CLOSED / COMPLETED`，但从业务语义看还不够清晰，尤其你已经引入了“交付准备 / 交付执行”流程后：

- `CLOSED` 现在同时承担了两层含义：
  1. 已截单（顾客不能再点）
  2. 正在交付/待收款（配送执行阶段）

这会让页面文案和状态判断变得含糊。  
建议把 `sale` 生命周期明确成你说的 4 阶段（外加草稿）：

- `DRAFT`（草稿，店主编辑中）
- `OPEN`（开单中，可下单）
- `CLOSED`（已截单，禁止再点单，待进入交付执行）
- `FULFILLING`（交付中）
- `COMPLETED`（完成）

这样 UI、云函数规则、复盘筛选、交付页面权限都会更清晰。

---

## 现状（已确认）
当前代码里已经存在：
- `DRAFT / OPEN / CLOSED`
- 我们新增了 `COMPLETED`

并且已有逻辑大量判断：
- 顾客下单/改单只允许 `sale.status === 'OPEN'`
- 交付准备/交付执行当前允许 `CLOSED` 和 `COMPLETED`
- `completeSaleFulfillment` 目前是从 `CLOSED -> COMPLETED`

所以要加 `FULFILLING`，会影响：
- 云函数 `admin`
- 交付页状态机
- 首页展示文案
- 复盘和交付 sale 列表筛选

---

## 目标状态机（建议定稿）

### Sale 状态（最终）
- `DRAFT`：草稿（未开单）
- `OPEN`：开单中（顾客可下单）
- `CLOSED`：已截单（顾客不能下单），尚未进入交付执行（或未正式开始）
- `FULFILLING`：交付中（店主开始执行交付/收款）
- `COMPLETED`：交付和收款全部完成

### 状态迁移（建议）
- `DRAFT -> OPEN`（开单）
- `OPEN -> CLOSED`（截单）
- `CLOSED -> FULFILLING`（开始交付，首次进入执行页操作时自动触发，或手动按钮触发）
- `FULFILLING -> COMPLETED`（店主点击“标记完成”，后端校验）
- `COMPLETED` 不再回退（第一版不支持撤销）

> 我建议 **`CLOSED -> FULFILLING` 在执行页第一次执行订单操作时自动触发**，这样店主不需要多按一步，状态又能真实反映业务阶段。  
> 如果你更喜欢显式控制，也可加“开始交付”按钮。下文我会给出两种方案，默认推荐自动触发。

---

## 为什么值得做（核心价值）
### 1) 状态语义清晰
- `CLOSED` 只表示“禁止点单”
- `FULFILLING` 才表示“配送/自取进行中”

### 2) 页面权限更自然
- 交付准备页：`CLOSED` 可编辑排序；`FULFILLING/COMPLETED` 通常只读（或 `FULFILLING` 仍可小改，见下）
- 交付执行页：`FULFILLING` 可操作；`COMPLETED` 只读

### 3) 首页和复盘页显示更可读
店主看到的是业务状态而不是技术状态：
- 开单中 / 已截单 / 配送中 / 完成

---

## 关键实现决策（需要锁定）

我先给你推荐默认值（如果你认可我就按这个方向出下一步执行计划）：

### A. `CLOSED -> FULFILLING` 如何触发？
- **推荐：自动触发**
- 触发点：`updateOrderFulfillmentProgress` 第一次成功更新某个订单交付/收款状态时
- 好处：店主不用额外点按钮，状态自然切换

备选：
- 手动“开始交付”按钮（更显式，但多一步操作）

### B. 交付准备页在 `FULFILLING` 时是否还能改排序？
- **推荐：允许继续改排序（但提示“交付中，修改会影响后续顺序”）**
- 因为真实场景配送途中路线可能变
- 你之前说“店主自由度最高”，这也符合

备选：
- `FULFILLING` 锁死排序，只能 `CLOSED` 改（更严谨但不够灵活）

### C. 交付执行页允许哪些 sale 状态进入？
- **推荐：`CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`**
  - `CLOSED`：可开始执行（首次操作转 `FULFILLING`）
  - `FULFILLING`：正常执行
  - `COMPLETED`：只读查看
- 不允许 `OPEN / DRAFT`

### D. 复盘页是否显示 `FULFILLING`
- **推荐：显示**
- 因为店主可能在配送中就要看阶段性统计

---

## 需要修改的地方（实施面）

## 1) 后端：`cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`
### 需要新增常量
在 `SALE_STATUS` 里加入：
- `FULFILLING: 'FULFILLING'`

### 需要调整的 action（重点）
#### `listFulfillmentSales`
当前筛选是 `CLOSED / COMPLETED`
- 改为：`CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`

#### `getSaleFulfillmentPrep`
当前允许：
- `CLOSED / COMPLETED`
建议改为：
- `CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`
并返回 `canEdit` 规则（按你的偏好定）
- 若采用我推荐：`CLOSED` 和 `FULFILLING` 都可编辑；`COMPLETED` 不可编辑
- 若保守：仅 `CLOSED` 可编辑

#### `saveSaleFulfillmentOrder`
当前只允许 `CLOSED`
如果采用“FULFILLING 也允许改排序”：
- 改为允许 `CLOSED / FULFILLING`
否则保持 `CLOSED`

#### `getSaleFulfillmentRun`
当前允许：
- `CLOSED / COMPLETED`
改为：
- `CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`
并 `canOperate` 规则改成：
- `sale.status === 'CLOSED' || sale.status === 'FULFILLING'`

#### `updateOrderFulfillmentProgress`（关键）
当前要求 sale 必须 `CLOSED`
建议改成：
- 若 `COMPLETED`：拒绝（保持）
- 若 `CLOSED`：允许，并在本次更新成功时自动把 sale 状态改为 `FULFILLING`
- 若 `FULFILLING`：允许正常更新
- 其他状态：拒绝

并在审计日志里可记录：
- 首次进入交付阶段时写一条 `SALE_START_FULFILLING`（可选）

#### `completeSaleFulfillment`
当前要求 sale.status === `CLOSED`
改为：
- 允许 `FULFILLING`（推荐主路径）
- 是否允许 `CLOSED` 直接完成？
  - **推荐允许**（如果店主全部自取且已逐单处理完，但状态尚未切到 `FULFILLING` 的边界情况）
  - 但如果采用“自动首单操作转 `FULFILLING`”，通常实际会是 `FULFILLING`

### 可选新增 action（若你想显式按钮）
- `startSaleFulfillment`
  - `CLOSED -> FULFILLING`
  - 但如果采用自动触发，就不需要新增这个 action

---

## 2) 前端：交付准备页（`pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.*`）
### 状态显示文案优化
把当前生硬的 `sale.status` 显示成中文：
- `CLOSED` -> 已截单
- `FULFILLING` -> 配送中 / 交付中
- `COMPLETED` -> 完成

### `canEdit` 文案与按钮
根据最终规则决定：
- 若 `FULFILLING` 可编辑：
  - 显示提示：`交付中，调整排序会影响后续执行顺序`
- 若不可编辑：
  - 显示提示：`交付已开始，排序已锁定`

---

## 3) 前端：交付执行页（`pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.*`）
### 状态显示文案优化
同上，给 `sale.status` 做中文映射

### 操作态 `canOperate`
由后端 `canOperate` 驱动即可，但文案要和 `FULFILLING` 一致：
- `CLOSED`：可操作（首次操作后进入交付中）
- `FULFILLING`：可操作
- `COMPLETED`：只读

### （可选）显示“已进入交付中”
如果采用自动触发，可以在首次操作成功后 toast：
- `已进入交付中`

---

## 4) 前端：店主首页、复盘页、其他列表（显示层）
这批改动不是功能必须，但建议同步改文案映射（避免显示英文状态）：
- `pages/admin/home/index.wxml` 当前开单卡片状态字段
- `pages/admin/export/index` 选择开单列表 label（可能出现 `FULFILLING/COMPLETED`）
- `pages/admin/orders/index` 若有展示 sale 状态的地方（当前主要展示订单状态，影响较小）

---

## Public API / Types 变更（若实施本方案）
### `sale.status` 枚举扩展
```ts
type SaleStatus = 'DRAFT' | 'OPEN' | 'CLOSED' | 'FULFILLING' | 'COMPLETED'
```

### `admin` 云函数行为变更（兼容性）
- `listFulfillmentSales`：返回列表可能包含 `FULFILLING`
- `getSaleFulfillmentPrep` / `getSaleFulfillmentRun`：接受 `FULFILLING`
- `updateOrderFulfillmentProgress`：成功时可能触发 sale 状态从 `CLOSED` 自动变 `FULFILLING`
- `completeSaleFulfillment`：允许从 `FULFILLING` 完成

---

## 测试场景（验收重点）

### A. 状态迁移
1. `OPEN -> CLOSED`（截单）后状态仍正常

<proposed_plan>
## 重构 Sale 生命周期状态（从“开单/截单”扩展到“配送中/完成”的显式状态）

### Summary
你这个判断是对的。现在 `sale` 状态虽然技术上已有 `DRAFT / OPEN / CLOSED / COMPLETED`，但从业务语义看还不够清晰，尤其你已经引入了“交付准备 / 交付执行”流程后：

- `CLOSED` 现在同时承担了两层含义：
  1. 已截单（顾客不能再点）
  2. 正在交付/待收款（配送执行阶段）

这会让页面文案和状态判断变得含糊。  
建议把 `sale` 生命周期明确成你说的 4 阶段（外加草稿）：

- `DRAFT`（草稿，店主编辑中）
- `OPEN`（开单中，可下单）
- `CLOSED`（已截单，禁止再点单，待进入交付执行）
- `FULFILLING`（交付中）
- `COMPLETED`（完成）

这样 UI、云函数规则、复盘筛选、交付页面权限都会更清晰。

---

## 现状（已确认）
当前代码里已经存在：
- `DRAFT / OPEN / CLOSED`
- 我们新增了 `COMPLETED`

并且已有逻辑大量判断：
- 顾客下单/改单只允许 `sale.status === 'OPEN'`
- 交付准备/交付执行当前允许 `CLOSED` 和 `COMPLETED`
- `completeSaleFulfillment` 目前是从 `CLOSED -> COMPLETED`

所以要加 `FULFILLING`，会影响：
- 云函数 `admin`
- 交付页状态机
- 首页展示文案
- 复盘和交付 sale 列表筛选

---

## 目标状态机（建议定稿）

### Sale 状态（最终）
- `DRAFT`：草稿（未开单）
- `OPEN`：开单中（顾客可下单）
- `CLOSED`：已截单（顾客不能下单），尚未进入交付执行（或未正式开始）
- `FULFILLING`：交付中（店主开始执行交付/收款）
- `COMPLETED`：交付和收款全部完成

### 状态迁移（建议）
- `DRAFT -> OPEN`（开单）
- `OPEN -> CLOSED`（截单）
- `CLOSED -> FULFILLING`（开始交付，首次进入执行页操作时自动触发，或手动按钮触发）
- `FULFILLING -> COMPLETED`（店主点击“标记完成”，后端校验）
- `COMPLETED` 不再回退（第一版不支持撤销）

> 我建议 **`CLOSED -> FULFILLING` 在执行页第一次执行订单操作时自动触发**，这样店主不需要多按一步，状态又能真实反映业务阶段。  
> 如果你更喜欢显式控制，也可加“开始交付”按钮。下文我会给出两种方案，默认推荐自动触发。

---

## 为什么值得做（核心价值）
### 1) 状态语义清晰
- `CLOSED` 只表示“禁止点单”
- `FULFILLING` 才表示“配送/自取进行中”

### 2) 页面权限更自然
- 交付准备页：`CLOSED` 可编辑排序；`FULFILLING/COMPLETED` 通常只读（或 `FULFILLING` 仍可小改，见下）
- 交付执行页：`FULFILLING` 可操作；`COMPLETED` 只读

### 3) 首页和复盘页显示更可读
店主看到的是业务状态而不是技术状态：
- 开单中 / 已截单 / 配送中 / 完成

---

## 关键实现决策（需要锁定）

我先给你推荐默认值（如果你认可我就按这个方向出下一步执行计划）：

### A. `CLOSED -> FULFILLING` 如何触发？
- **推荐：自动触发**
- 触发点：`updateOrderFulfillmentProgress` 第一次成功更新某个订单交付/收款状态时
- 好处：店主不用额外点按钮，状态自然切换

备选：
- 手动“开始交付”按钮（更显式，但多一步操作）

### B. 交付准备页在 `FULFILLING` 时是否还能改排序？
- **推荐：允许继续改排序（但提示“交付中，修改会影响后续顺序”）**
- 因为真实场景配送途中路线可能变
- 你之前说“店主自由度最高”，这也符合

备选：
- `FULFILLING` 锁死排序，只能 `CLOSED` 改（更严谨但不够灵活）

### C. 交付执行页允许哪些 sale 状态进入？
- **推荐：`CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`**
  - `CLOSED`：可开始执行（首次操作转 `FULFILLING`）
  - `FULFILLING`：正常执行
  - `COMPLETED`：只读查看
- 不允许 `OPEN / DRAFT`

### D. 复盘页是否显示 `FULFILLING`
- **推荐：显示**
- 因为店主可能在配送中就要看阶段性统计

---

## 1) 后端：`cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`
### 需要新增常量
在 `SALE_STATUS` 里加入：
- `FULFILLING: 'FULFILLING'`

#### `listFulfillmentSales`
当前筛选是 `CLOSED / COMPLETED`
- 改为：`CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`

#### `getSaleFulfillmentPrep`
当前允许：
- `CLOSED / COMPLETED`
建议改为：
- `CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`
并返回 `canEdit` 规则（按你的偏好定）
- 若采用我推荐：`CLOSED` 和 `FULFILLING` 都可编辑；`COMPLETED` 不可编辑
- 若保守：仅 `CLOSED` 可编辑

#### `saveSaleFulfillmentOrder`
当前只允许 `CLOSED`
如果采用“FULFILLING 也允许改排序”：
- 改为允许 `CLOSED / FULFILLING`
否则保持 `CLOSED`

#### `getSaleFulfillmentRun`
当前允许：
- `CLOSED / COMPLETED`
改为：
- `CLOSED / FULFILLING / COMPLETED`
并 `canOperate` 规则改成：
- `sale.status === 'CLOSED' || sale.status === 'FULFILLING'`

#### `updateOrderFulfillmentProgress`（关键）
当前要求 sale 必须 `CLOSED`
建议改成：
- 若 `COMPLETED`：拒绝（保持）
- 若 `CLOSED`：允许，并在本次更新成功时自动把 sale 状态改为 `FULFILLING`
- 若 `FULFILLING`：允许正常更新
- 其他状态：拒绝

并在审计日志里可记录：
- 首次进入交付阶段时写一条 `SALE_START_FULFILLING`（可选）

#### `completeSaleFulfillment`
当前要求 sale.status === `CLOSED`
改为：
- 允许 `FULFILLING`（推荐主路径）
- 是否允许 `CLOSED` 直接完成？
  - **推荐允许**（如果店主全部自取且已逐单处理完，但状态尚未切到 `FULFILLING` 的边界情况）
  - 但如果采用“自动首单操作转 `FULFILLING`”，通常实际会是 `FULFILLING`

### 可选新增 action（若你想显式按钮）

  - `CLOSED -> FULFILLING`
  - 但如果采用自动触发，就不需要新增这个 action

---

- `COMPLETED` -> 完成

- 若不可编辑：
  - 显示提示：`交付已开始，排序已锁定`

---

## 3) 前端：交付执行页（`pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.*`）
### 状态显示文案优化

由后端 `canOperate` 驱动即可，但文案要和 `FULFILLING` 一致：

这批改动不是功能必须，但建议同步改文案映射（避免显示英文状态）：

payload.message:
已实现。现在 `sale` 状态语义变成这套：

- `DRAFT` 草稿
- `OPEN` 开单中
- `CLOSED` 已截单（禁止再点单）
- `FULFILLING` 配送中 / 交付中
- `COMPLETED` 完成

**本次改动（核心）**
- `cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`
  - 新增 `SALE_STATUS.FULFILLING`
  - 交付相关接口支持 `FULFILLING`
  - `updateOrderFulfillmentProgress` 在 `CLOSED` 状态下首次成功操作订单时，自动把 sale 切到 `FULFILLING`
  - `completeSaleFulfillment` 支持从 `CLOSED / FULFILLING` 完成到 `COMPLETED`
- `pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.js`
  - 默认选单时会优先 `CLOSED`，其次 `FULFILLING`
  - `FULFILLING` 状态也允许调整排序（符合你“店主自由度高”）
  - 状态文案改成中文显示（如“已截单 / 配送中 / 完成”）
- `pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.wxml`
  - 显示中文状态
  - `FULFILLING` 时提示“配送进行中，调整排序会影响后续执行顺序”
- `pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js`
  - 默认选单优先 `CLOSED`，其次 `FULFILLING`
  - 收到后端状态切换回执时，首次操作会提示“已进入配送中”

<collaboration_mode># Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).

   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.

2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).

4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + file path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):

# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

能，基本能定位到一个**高概率源头**，而且就在代码里。

**我目前判断的最可能原因**
- 在 `cloudfunctions/admin/index.js` 的 `saveSaleFulfillmentPlan(...)` 里，创建新文档时用了：
  - `db.collection('saleFulfillmentPlans').doc(id).set(...)`
- 但同时 `data` 里又手动写了：
  - `_id: id`

也就是同一份写入里既用 `doc(id)` 指定文档 ID，又在 `data` 里再写 `_id`。  
这在 CloudBase 里很容易导致 `document.set:fail ...`（常见是 `_id` 相关写入冲突/非法写字段）。

你可以看这里（我刚定位到）：
- `cloudfunctions/admin/index.js:228`
- `cloudfunctions/admin/index.js:230`

大致是这段：
- `doc(id).set({ data: { _id: id, ... } })`

**为什么我觉得不是“表不存在”**
- 你已经建了 `saleFulfillmentPlans`
- 我之前还专门加了“集合不存在”的提示分支，如果是这个问题，前端提示通常会是“请先创建数据库集合 saleFulfillmentPlans”
- 你现在看到的是通用 `save fulfillment order failed`，更像是进入了 catch 的其它错误

**还需要你确认一下（用于100%锁定）**
请贴一下这次“保存排序”对应的 **admin 云函数日志**里的具体错误行（`document.set:fail ...` 那段）。  
如果日志里看到 `_id` / `document.set` 相关报错，那就完全坐实了。

你先发日志，我再给你一个统一修正计划（你说了等你说 ok 再统一修正 plan）。

这个我懂，是微信开发者工具日志日期筛选的坑，不是你操作问题。

在看不到日志的前提下，我先给你一个**基于代码的高置信判断**（不改代码，只定位）：

## 高概率根因（>80%）
`saveSaleFulfillmentPlan()` 新建排序计划文档时，代码同时做了这两件事：
- 用 `doc(id)` 指定文档 ID
- 在 `data` 里又写 `_id: id`

CloudBase 很多场景下不允许你在 `set/update` 的 `data` 里显式写 `_id`（尤其你已经通过 `doc(id)` 指定了主键），会直接 `document.set:fail`。

也就是说，第一次保存排序（表里还没有这条计划）最容易炸。  
如果这条文档已经存在，走 `update` 分支，反而可能正常。

---

## 你现在可以做一个“无日志验证”（不改代码）

# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

payload.message:
这个我大概率能直接定位到，**是前端事件里一个典型的 `0` 被当成 false 的 bug**。

## 根因（高概率）
在 `pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js` 的 `onOrderAction(e)` 里，索引读取写法是这种模式：

- `Number((e.currentTarget.dataset && e.currentTarget.dataset.idx) || -1)`

问题在于：
- 当你点的是**第 1 条订单**时，`idx = 0`
- `0` 在 JS 里是 falsy
- 所以表达式会变成 `0 || -1`，结果是 `-1`
- 后面代码发现 `idx < 0`，直接 `return`
- 表现出来就是：**点“操作”没反应**

也就是说：
- 很可能**第一条点不动**
- 第二条、第三条可能能弹出（如果你有多条单）

---

## 你现在可以立刻验证（不改代码）
试一下：
1. 在交付执行页点 **第2条订单** 的“操作”
2. 如果第2条能弹出 action sheet，而第1条不行，那就完全坐实了

---

## 顺手提醒（同类 bug 可能还有）
同样的写法在 `交付准备页` 的 `上移/下移` 也用了索引读取：
- `data-idx="{{index}}"` + `|| -1`
所以：
- **第1条“下移”也可能没反应**（同一个原因）

---

这个问题我已经定位到了。你继续说下一个 bug。  
等你说 `ok`，我再统一给修正 plan。

A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and file path so you can open the source for full instructions when using a specific skill.
### Available skills
- skill-creator: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations. (file: C:/Users/hanch/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: C:/Users/hanch/.codex/skills/.system/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + file path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, open its `SKILL.md`. Read only enough to follow the workflow.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the skill directory listed above first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, load only the specific files needed for the request; don't bulk-load everything.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Keep context small: summarize long sections instead of pasting them; only load extra files when needed.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.

## 交付流程首轮 Bug 修复计划（保存排序失败 + 执行页“操作”按钮无响应）

### Summary
针对你刚刚确认的两个问题，做一轮集中修复：

1. **交付准备页保存排序失败**
- 高概率根因是云函数新建 `saleFulfillmentPlans` 文档时，`doc(id).set()` 与 `data._id` 重复指定主键导致 CloudBase `document.set:fail`
- 修复为：使用 `doc(id).set()` 时 **不再在 `data` 中写 `_id`**

2. **交付执行页点“操作”没反应**
- 根因是前端从 `dataset.idx` 读取索引时使用 `|| -1`，导致首行 `index=0` 被当作 falsy 并误判为 `-1`
- 修复为：安全读取 `dataset.idx`，保留 `0`

同时顺手修复同类问题（交付准备页上移/下移按钮的 `index=0` 读取）。

---

## 已定位问题与根因（结论）

### Bug 1：交付准备页保存排序失败（`save fulfillment order failed`）
#### 高概率根因（已通过代码定位）
文件：`cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`  
函数：`saveSaleFulfillmentPlan(saleId, orderIds, openId)`

当前新建分支使用了：
- `db.collection('saleFulfillmentPlans').doc(id).set(...)`
并且 `data` 里又写：
- `_id: id`

这会导致 CloudBase 在部分情况下报 `document.set:fail`（主键冲突/非法写 `_id`）。

#### 修复策略（决定）
- 保留 `doc(id).set(...)`
- **删除 `data._id` 字段**
- 返回值仍然可在内存中拼出 `_id: id`（不影响调用方）

---

### Bug 2：交付执行页“操作”按钮点了没反应
#### 根因（已定位）
文件：`pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js`  
函数：`onOrderAction(e)`

当前写法等价于：
```js
const idx = Number(dataset.idx || -1)
```
当 `dataset.idx = 0`（第一条订单）时：
- `0 || -1 => -1`
- 触发 `idx < 0` 返回
- 所以第一条订单点“操作”无响应

#### 修复策略（决定）
用“是否存在字段”的方式读取，而不是 `||`：
```js
const rawIdx = e.currentTarget.dataset ? e.currentTarget.dataset.idx : undefined
const idx = rawIdx === undefined ? -1 : Number(rawIdx)
```
或等价写法（关键点：不能把 `0` 当 false）。

---

### 同类 Bug（顺手修复）
#### 交付准备页 `上移/下移`
文件：`pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.js`
- `onMoveUp`
- `onMoveDown`

也用了同类写法：
- `Number(dataset.idx || -1)`

同样会让 `index=0` 的读取异常（尤其“下移第一条”会无响应）。
本次一并修复，避免你下一步再撞一次。

---

## 变更范围（精确）

### 后端
- `cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`
  - `saveSaleFulfillmentPlan()` 新建文档分支去掉 `data._id`

### 前端
- `pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js`
  - `onOrderAction()` 的 `dataset.idx` 读取方式修复
- `pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.js`
  - `onMoveUp()` 的 `dataset.idx` 读取方式修复
  - `onMoveDown()` 的 `dataset.idx` 读取方式修复

---

## 实现细节（决定版）

### 1) `cloudfunctions/admin/index.js` 修复 `_id` 重复写入
#### 当前问题代码（概念）
```js
db.collection('saleFulfillmentPlans').doc(id).set({
  data: {
    _id: id,
    ...
  }
})
```

#### 修改后
```js
db.collection('saleFulfillmentPlans').doc(id).set({
  data: {
    ...
  }
})
```

#### 返回值保持兼容
函数返回仍可保留：
```js
return { _id: id, ...payload }
```
这样上层不用改。

---

### 2) `pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js` 修复 `onOrderAction`
#### 修改点
- 替换 `idx` 读取逻辑，确保 `0` 不丢失

#### 行为结果
- 第一条订单点击“操作”可以正常弹出 action sheet
- 其他行行为不变

---

### 3) `pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.js` 修复 `onMoveUp/onMoveDown`
#### 修改点
- 同样替换 `dataset.idx` 的读取逻辑

#### 行为结果
- 第一条订单的“下移”不再因为 `idx=0` 被误判
- “上移”逻辑仍会正确拦截 `idx<=0`

---

## 测试用例（本轮修复验收）

### A. 保存排序失败修复
1. **首次保存排序（该 sale 尚无排序计划文档）**
- 进入交付准备页
- 不改顺序直接点“保存排序”
- 预期：保存成功，不再出现 `save fulfillment order failed`

2. **再次保存（已有排序计划文档）**
- 调整顺序后再次保存
- 预期：保存成功

3. **空订单列表**
- 无有效订单时保存按钮不可用（现有规则）
- 预期：无异常

---

### B. 交付执行页“操作”按钮修复
4. **点击第1条订单的“操作”**
- 预期：弹出 action sheet（之前无响应）

5. **点击第2条/第3条订单**
- 预期：仍正常弹出 action sheet（回归）

---

### C. 交付准备页同类索引问题修复
6. **第1条订单点“下移”**
- 预期：顺序变化成功（之前可能无响应）

7. **第1条订单点“上移”**
- 预期：仍正确无动作（逻辑拦截，不报错）

---

## 回归范围（简短）
- 交付执行页其它按钮行为（操作后刷新列表）不变
- 保存排序后再次打开交付准备页顺序仍能回显
- 不影响 `saleFulfillmentPlans` 读取、交付执行、完成开单逻辑

---

## 部署与发布影响
### 需要重新部署
- `admin` 云函数（因为修了 `saveSaleFulfillmentPlan`）

### 需要重新编译
- 小程序前端（因为修了两个页面的 `dataset.idx` 读取）

### 数据库
- 不需要新增表（你已有 `saleFulfillmentPlans`）
- 不需要清库

---

## Assumptions / Defaults
- 这轮只修你已确认的两类 bug，不顺带调整其它交付流程交互
- 保存排序失败的根因按当前代码高置信认定为 `_id` 重复写入；如果修复后仍失败，再看云端日志做第二轮定位
- `dataset.idx` 读取统一采用“显式判断 `undefined`”方案，避免未来再被 `0` 坑一次

settings.developer_instructions:
# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

## Two kinds of unknowns (treat differently)

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types

# Plan Mode (Conversational)

You work in 3 phases, and you should *chat your way* to a great plan before finalizing it. A great plan is very detailed—intent- and implementation-wise—so that it can be handed to another engineer or agent to be implemented right away. It must be **decision complete**, where the implementer does not need to make any decisions.

## Mode rules (strict)

You are in **Plan Mode** until a developer message explicitly ends it.

Plan Mode is not changed by user intent, tone, or imperative language. If a user asks for execution while still in Plan Mode, treat it as a request to **plan the execution**, not perform it.

## Plan Mode vs update_plan tool

Plan Mode is a collaboration mode that can involve requesting user input and eventually issuing a `<proposed_plan>` block.

Separately, `update_plan` is a checklist/progress/TODOs tool; it does not enter or exit Plan Mode. Do not confuse it with Plan mode or try to use it while in Plan mode. If you try to use `update_plan` in Plan mode, it will return an error.

## Execution vs. mutation in Plan Mode

You may explore and execute **non-mutating** actions that improve the plan. You must not perform **mutating** actions.

### Allowed (non-mutating, plan-improving)

Actions that gather truth, reduce ambiguity, or validate feasibility without changing repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Reading or searching files, configs, schemas, types, manifests, and docs
* Static analysis, inspection, and repo exploration
* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files
* Tests, builds, or checks that may write to caches or build artifacts (for example, `target/`, `.cache/`, or snapshots) so long as they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files
* Running formatters or linters that rewrite files
* Applying patches, migrations, or codegen that updates repo-tracked files
* Side-effectful commands whose purpose is to carry out the plan rather than refine it

When in doubt: if the action would reasonably be described as "doing the work" rather than "planning the work," do not do it.

## PHASE 1 — Ground in the environment (explore first, ask second)

Begin by grounding yourself in the actual environment. Eliminate unknowns in the prompt by discovering facts, not by asking the user. Resolve all questions that can be answered through exploration or inspection. Identify missing or ambiguous details only if they cannot be derived from the environment. Silent exploration between turns is allowed and encouraged.

Before asking the user any question, perform at least one targeted non-mutating exploration pass (for example: search relevant files, inspect likely entrypoints/configs, confirm current implementation shape), unless no local environment/repo is available.

Exception: you may ask clarifying questions about the user's prompt before exploring, ONLY if there are obvious ambiguities or contradictions in the prompt itself. However, if ambiguity might be resolved by exploring, always prefer exploring first.

Do not ask questions that can be answered from the repo or system (for example, "where is this struct?" or "which UI component should we use?" when exploration can make it clear). Only ask once you have exhausted reasonable non-mutating exploration.

## PHASE 2 — Intent chat (what they actually want)

* Keep asking until you can clearly state: goal + success criteria, audience, in/out of scope, constraints, current state, and the key preferences/tradeoffs.
* Bias toward questions over guessing: if any high-impact ambiguity remains, do NOT plan yet—ask.

## PHASE 3 — Implementation chat (what/how we’ll build)

* Once intent is stable, keep asking until the spec is decision complete: approach, interfaces (APIs/schemas/I/O), data flow, edge cases/failure modes, testing + acceptance criteria, rollout/monitoring, and any migrations/compat constraints.

## Asking questions

Critical rules:

* Strongly prefer using the `request_user_input` tool to ask any questions.
* Offer only meaningful multiple‑choice options; don’t include filler choices that are obviously wrong or irrelevant.
* In rare cases where an unavoidable, important question can’t be expressed with reasonable multiple‑choice options (due to extreme ambiguity), you may ask it directly without the tool.

You SHOULD ask many questions, but each question must:

* materially change the spec/plan, OR
* confirm/lock an assumption, OR
* choose between meaningful tradeoffs.
* not be answerable by non-mutating commands.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for decisions that materially change the plan, for confirming important assumptions, or for information that cannot be discovered via non-mutating exploration.

1. **Discoverable facts** (repo/system truth): explore first.

   * Before asking, run targeted searches and check likely sources of truth (configs/manifests/entrypoints/schemas/types/constants).
   * Ask only if: multiple plausible candidates; nothing found but you need a missing identifier/context; or ambiguity is actually product intent.
   * If asking, present concrete candidates (paths/service names) + recommend one.
   * Never ask questions you can answer from your environment (e.g., “where is this struct”).

2. **Preferences/tradeoffs** (not discoverable): ask early.

   * These are intent or implementation preferences that cannot be derived from exploration.
   * Provide 2–4 mutually exclusive options + a recommended default.
   * If unanswered, proceed with the recommended option and record it as an assumption in the final plan.

## Finalization rule

Only output the final plan when it is decision complete and leaves no decisions to the implementer.

When you present the official plan, wrap it in a `<proposed_plan>` block so the client can render it specially:

1) The opening tag must be on its own line.
2) Start the plan content on the next line (no text on the same line as the tag).
3) The closing tag must be on its own line.
4) Use Markdown inside the block.
5) Keep the tags exactly as `<proposed_plan>` and `</proposed_plan>` (do not translate or rename them), even if the plan content is in another language.

Example:

<proposed_plan>
plan content
</proposed_plan>

plan content should be human and agent digestible. The final plan must be plan-only and include:

* A clear title
* A brief summary section
* Important changes or additions to public APIs/interfaces/types
* Test cases and scenarios
* Explicit assumptions and defaults chosen where needed

Do not ask "should I proceed?" in the final output. The user can easily switch out of Plan mode and request implementation if you have included a `<proposed_plan>` block in your response. Alternatively, they can decide to stay in Plan mode and continue refining the plan.

Only produce at most one `<proposed_plan>` block per turn, and only when you are presenting a complete spec.

* Dry-run style commands when they do not edit repo-tracked files

### Not allowed (mutating, plan-executing)

Actions that implement the plan or change repo-tracked state. Examples:

* Editing or writing files

### 1) 交付准备页“保存排序”失败（`save fulfillment order failed`）
#### 高概率根因
文件：`cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`  
函数：`saveSaleFulfillmentPlan()`

当前创建新文档时：
- 已用 `doc(id)` 指定文档 ID
- 同时在 `data` 里写 `_id: id`

CloudBase 常见会因此报 `document.set:fail`。

#### 修复策略（锁定）
- 保留 `doc(id).set(...)`
- 删除 `data._id`
- 返回值可继续在函数里拼 `_id: id`（不影响前端）

### 2) 交付执行页“操作”没反应（尤其第一条）

文件：`pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js`  
函数：`onOrderAction()`

使用 `Number(dataset.idx || -1)` 导致：
- 第一条 `idx=0` 被当成 falsy
- 变成 `-1`，直接 return

#### 修复策略（锁定）
- 显式判断 `undefined` 再 `Number(...)`
- 同类问题一并修复到交付准备页：

  - `onMoveDown()`

### 新需求（已确认）
- 店主端订单详情页支持改付款方式

  - `现金`
  - `转账`
- 交互用 `picker`（你已选）

#### A. 新增 admin 云函数 action（推荐）

- `updateOrderPayment`

```js
{
  orderId: string,
  paymentMethod?: 'cash' | 'wechat_transfer',
  paidStatus?: 'UNPAID' | 'PAID'
}
```

用途：
- 店主订单详情页改付款方式
- 也可以给交付执行页快捷切换 `💰` 复用（只传 `paidStatus`）

> 这样能避免“付款相关状态”散落在多个 action 里。

#### B. 店主订单详情页前端
文件：
- `pages/admin/order-detail/index.js`
- `pages/admin/order-detail/index.wxml`

新增能力：
- 在付款卡片加 `picker`（现金 / 转账）
- 保存逻辑并入现有“保存修改”流程或单独“保存付款方式”按钮（二选一）

- 在付款卡片增加：
  - `picker` 选择付款方式
  - `保存付款方式` 小按钮（单独提交）

- `wechat_transfer`（转账）

- `PENDING` → `DELIVERED`
- `DELIVERED` → `PENDING`（建议支持回退，防止误点）

### 调用后端
复用 `admin.updateOrderFulfillmentProgress`（已存在）：
```js
{ orderId, saleId, handoffStatus: nextStatus }
```

### UI反馈
- 成功后 toast：`已标记送达` / `已撤销送达`
- 刷新当前执行列表（沿用现有 `loadRun()`）

---

## 2) `💰` 按钮（收款状态切换）
### 当前行状态 → 下一状态
- `UNPAID` → `PAID`
- `PAID` → `UNPAID`（建议支持回退，防止误点）

### 调用后端（推荐统一）
调用新 `admin.updateOrderPayment`：
```js
{ orderId, paidStatus: nextStatus }
```
或者直接继续用 `updateOrderFulfillmentProgress`：
```js
{ orderId, saleId, paidStatus: nextStatus }
```

#### 最终建议（为了少改）
- **继续复用 `updateOrderFulfillmentProgress`**（本轮推荐）
- 原因：它已经有支付状态更新能力，不必再新增一个 action 才能满足执行页快捷按钮
- `updateOrderPayment` 仍然建议新增给订单详情页用（也可订单详情页复用同一 action，见下）

---

### 行为
- `bindtap="goOrderDetail"`
- 跳转：

### 注意事项（事件冒泡）
行内有 `🚚`、`💰` 按钮时，点按钮不能触发行点击跳转。
需要在按钮事件处理里：
- 使用 `catchtap`（推荐）
而不是 `bindtap`

这样：
- 点按钮只执行状态切换
- 点空白区域才进订单详情

而不是 `bindtap`

- 点按钮只执行状态切换
- 点空白区域才进订单详情

### Summary
你看到的两个问题都已定位为“时序与平台能力”问题，不是单点 bug：

1. **店主端按钮晚出现**  
   现在 `sync-guard` 只完成 `customer.bootstrapHome`。  
   但 `店主端`按钮依赖 `getSession()`（内部还会并行调 `auth.getMyOpenId` + `auth.isAdmin`），所以会在“同步完成后”再晚一拍才出现。

2. **同步后又跳“我的”页**  
   现在是首页先渲染，再在 `bootstrap()` 里判断 `profile.isComplete` 后导航，因此你会看到一次首页闪过。

## 实施策略（统一规范，避免每页各写一套）

### A. 统一状态约定（前端页面层）
对“需要首屏请求”的页面统一引入两个状态字段：
- `initialLoading: boolean`：首屏或首次进入页面时为 `true`
- `initialLoaded: boolean`：首屏请求完成后置 `true`

说明：
- 不用单纯依赖 `loading`，因为很多页面 `loading` 还会用于刷新/切换筛选；首屏逻辑和后续交互 loading 要分开。
- `initialLoaded` 用来避免“空态误闪”。

### B. WXML 渲染规则统一
页面内容区按以下顺序判断：
1. `wx:if="{{initialLoading}}"` → 显示“载入中...”卡片
2. `wx:elif="{{!initialLoading && 空数据}}"` → 显示真实空态（如“暂无订单”）
3. `wx:else` → 显示列表/表单正文

这样就不会出现：
- 先显示“暂无地址/暂无订单/暂无开单中”，过一会儿又变成有内容

### C. JS 请求流程统一
在每个页面的 `reload/init/onLoad` 内：
- 请求前：
  - 首次进入：`initialLoading=true`
  - 后续刷新：可只用 `loading=true`（不遮全页）
- 请求结束（成功或失败）：
  - `initialLoading=false`
  - `initialLoaded=true`
- 失败时：
  - 保持页面可见，toast 提示
  - 不把失败误渲染成“空数据”

你说的skeleton UI是啥玩意儿？业界对于这种问题通常是怎么做的？

`skeleton UI` 就是“骨架屏”。

简单说：
- 不是显示一行“载入中...”
- 而是先显示一版**页面结构的占位形状**
- 比如头像位置一个灰圆、标题一条灰块、列表几行灰条
- 数据回来后再替换成真实内容

你现在这个“我的”页如果用骨架屏，效果会像：
- 昵称输入框位置先是一条灰块
- 手机号输入框一条灰块
- 默认地址摘要区域一条灰块
- 按钮区域也是灰块

这样视觉上会更稳，不会有“空表单/内容突然跳出来”的感觉。

**业界通常怎么做（从常见到更高级）**
1. `Loading 文案/转圈`（最简单）
- 适合后台管理页、低频页面
- 成本低，但体验一般

2. `骨架屏（Skeleton）`（最常见）
- 适合列表页、详情页、个人页
- 用户会感觉“页面已经出来了，只是在填内容”
- 体验明显更好

3. `缓存旧数据 + 静默刷新`（体验最好）
- 先显示上次数据（snapshot / cache）
- 后台请求回来后无感更新
- 适合首页、个人页、订单页这类高频页面
- 但你刚刚已经决定这次先不扩 snapshot

4. `分层加载`
- 页面框架先出（导航、按钮）
- 重数据区域单独 loading / skeleton
- 避免全页被遮住

**你这个项目当前阶段，我建议**
- 先做我们刚讨论的：**统一“载入中...”状态**（快、稳、改动小）
- 后面如果你对某几个页面（如“我的”、菜单页、订单详情）还不满意，再升级成骨架屏

原因：
- 你现在还在频繁改逻辑，先把状态机理顺更重要
- 骨架屏主要提升观感，不解决逻辑问题
- 等结构稳定后再做骨架屏，不容易返工

如果你要，我后面可以给你一个很小的规范：哪些页面适合“文字loading”，哪些值得上骨架屏。
那我现在一部分数据用snapshot，一部分又要用loading，是不是有点乱

不乱，前提是你把规则定清楚。

这其实是业界常态：**缓存数据 + 实时请求** 混用。关键不是“是否混用”，而是“什么时候用哪种”。

你现在可以用一条很清晰的规则：

- `snapshot`：放**高频、跨页面、很多页面都会用**的数据
  - 例如：当前是否开单、当前菜单摘要、当前用户基础资料摘要、管理员身份
- 页面级 `loading`：放**这个页面独有**、进入页面才需要的数据
  - 例如：地址列表详情、订单列表、某个菜品编辑表单、导出页数据、起送价规则表单

这样不会乱，反而更合理。  
如果你把所有东西都塞 snapshot，才会变乱（臃肿、失效策略复杂、容易不同步）。

你现在的症状（“我的”页先空一下）本质不是“snapshot 和 loading 混用导致乱”，而是：
- 页面依赖的数据不在 snapshot
- 页面又没有明确 loading 态
- 所以出现“空壳闪现”

补上 loading 就正常了。

**一个实用判断标准（你后面都按这个来）**
- 这个数据会不会被 3 个以上页面复用？
  - 会：考虑进 snapshot
  - 不会：页面自己请求 + loading
- 这个数据大不大 / 变动频繁不频繁？
  - 大、细节多、变动频繁：别进 snapshot
- 没这个数据页面还能不能先稳定展示框架？
  - 能：页面级 loading 就够
  - 不能：考虑 snapshot 或路由前预加载

所以你现在这个方案是合理的，不是乱。  
你只需要把“边界”固定住，后续就顺。
行吧照你说的做吧

## 修复结算页删除地址后的短暂旧地址闪动（返回后立即去旧状态）

### Summary
在现有 `checkout_profile_dirty` 机制基础上升级为“带原因的脏标记（dirty payload）”，让结算页在 `onShow()` 检测到“删除地址”时，先做一次**本地同步修正（optimistic local reconcile）**，再静默向云端刷新资料。  
这样用户从地址管理返回结算页时，不会先看到旧地址再变成自取。

## 根因（当前行为）
- 当前 dirty 标记只有布尔含义：`checkout_profile_dirty = '1'`
- 结算页知道“资料变脏了”，但不知道“到底发生了什么”
- 因此只能异步 `reload()`，无法在云端响应前先清理本地旧地址状态
- 结果：短暂显示旧地址 → 再变成正确状态（自取）

  - 读取 `checkout_profile_dirty`

   - `recomputeAddressRuleHint()`
   - `recomputeSubmitDisabled()`

这样可以在云端返回前先去掉“明显错误”的旧地址展示。

3. `consumeCheckoutProfileDirty()`

这个错误大概率**不是你业务代码里的错误**，也**不是我写的 `sync-guard` 组件报的错**。

你看到的：

- `received error code 1 on sync-0`

更像是 **微信开发者工具 / 真机调试 的底层“文件同步通道”报错**（`sync-0` 可以理解为某个同步通道编号），属于工具链层面的通用错误，`code 1` 也通常是**泛化失败码**，不是业务语义错误。

**先区分两类“同步”**
- 我们代码里的 `sync-guard`：页面数据同步（会显示“同步失败/重试”）
- 你这个 `sync-0`：开发者工具把代码/资源同步到运行环境时的底层通道报错（IDE层）

**常见原因（按概率）**
1. 开发者工具/真机调试同步状态卡住（工具自身问题）
2. 项目里有大文件或频繁变化的文件被工具监控（你那个 `rollout-*.jsonl` 很可疑）
3. 某些文件被别的程序占用（杀毒、同步盘、编辑器插件）
4. 开发者工具缓存异常
5. 真机调试连接状态不稳定（USB/Wi-Fi 调试链路抖动）

**你先看它是不是“假报错”**
- 如果页面功能都正常，只是 console 偶发一条：大概率是工具同步抖了一下，可先忽略
- 如果伴随页面不刷新、白屏、样式不更新：那就是同步真的失败了

**不改代码的排查顺序（建议）**
1. 重新编译一次（不是热更新）
2. 关闭真机调试，再重新连接
3. 微信开发者工具：清缓存并重启
4. 暂时把项目根目录里那个 `rollout-*.jsonl` 移出去（至少不要让它在项目里变化）
5. 关掉可能占用项目目录的程序（同步盘/杀毒实时扫描）
6. 再试一次真机调试

**重点提醒**
- 这个错误信息本身不直接指向某一行代码
- 它更像“IDE同步失败”的信号，不是云函数报错、也不是小程序业务逻辑报错

## 数据模型与状态设计（核心）

### 1) `orders` 表新增字段（订单层）
#### 新增字段
- `handoffStatus: 'PENDING' | 'DELIVERED'`
  - `PENDING`：未交付（默认）
  - `DELIVERED`：货已交到客人手里（配送/自取统一）
- `handedOffAt: Date | null`
- `handedOffByOpenId: string | null`

#### 支付状态（复用现有）
- `order.payment.paidStatus: 'UNPAID' | 'PAID'`
- `order.payment.method: 'cash' | 'bank'`（沿用现有；若当前是 `transfer` 命名则保持实际代码命名）

#### 状态组合语义（执行流程）
- 现金交付完成：
  - `handoffStatus = DELIVERED`
  - `payment.paidStatus = PAID`
- 转账已交付未到账：
  - `handoffStatus = DELIVERED`
  - `payment.paidStatus = UNPAID`
- 转账到账后（回家后店主确认）：
  - `handoffStatus = DELIVERED`
  - `payment.paidStatus = PAID`

#### 初始化规则（创建订单时）
- 所有新订单默认：
  - `handoffStatus = 'PENDING'`
  - `payment.paidStatus` 继续沿用现有初始化逻辑（通常 `UNPAID`）

> 注意：`CANCELLED / REJECTED` 订单不参与交付流程。  
> `PENDING_REVIEW` 在截单后通常不应再进入交付；是否出现延后确认转有效见后文“新有效订单自动追加”规则。

---

### 2) `sales` 表状态扩展（sale 层）
#### 当前已有
- `DRAFT / OPEN / CLOSED`

#### 新增
- `COMPLETED`
  - 表示该 sale 的所有有效订单已完成交付且完成收款，店主已手动确认完结

#### 新增字段（推荐）
- `completedAt: Date | null`
- `completedByOpenId: string | null`

#### 状态流（本方案）
- `DRAFT -> OPEN -> CLOSED -> COMPLETED`

---

### 3) 新增独立表：交付排序表（你指定）
#### 集合名（推荐）
- `saleFulfillmentPlans`

> 如果你更喜欢中文语义也可以叫 `saleDeliveryPlans`，但本方案用 `saleFulfillmentPlans`（包含配送+自取）

#### 每个 sale 一条文档（推荐）
文档 ID 可直接用 `saleId`（推荐，查找最简单）：
- `_id = saleId`

#### 文档结构（建议定稿）

{
  _id: "<saleId>",
  saleId: "<saleId>",
  saleStatusSnapshot: "CLOSED", // 保存时记录，便于排查

## 目标状态机（建议定稿）

### Sale 状态（最终）
- `DRAFT`：草稿（未开单）
- `OPEN`：开单中（顾客可下单）
- `CLOSED`：已截单（顾客不能下单），尚未进入交付执行（或未正式开始）
- `FULFILLING`：交付中（店主开始执行交付/收款）
- `COMPLETED`：交付和收款全部完成

### 状态迁移（建议）
- `DRAFT -> OPEN`（开单）
- `OPEN -> CLOSED`（截单）
- `CLOSED -> FULFILLING`（开始交付，首次进入执行页操作时自动触发，或手动按钮触发）
- `FULFILLING -> COMPLETED`（店主点击“标记完成”，后端校验）
- `COMPLETED` 不再回退（第一版不支持撤销）

> 我建议 **`CLOSED -> FULFILLING` 在执行页第一次执行订单操作时自动触发**，这样店主不需要多按一步，状态又能真实反映业务阶段。

### Bug 1：交付准备页保存排序失败（`save fulfillment order failed`）
#### 高概率根因（已通过代码定位）
文件：`cloudfunctions/admin/index.js`  
函数：`saveSaleFulfillmentPlan(saleId, orderIds, openId)`

当前新建分支使用了：
- `db.collection('saleFulfillmentPlans').doc(id).set(...)`
并且 `data` 里又写：
- `_id: id`

这会导致 CloudBase 在部分情况下报 `document.set:fail`（主键冲突/非法写 `_id`）。

#### 修复策略（决定）
- 保留 `doc(id).set(...)`
- **删除 `data._id` 字段**
- 返回值仍然可在内存中拼出 `_id: id`（不影响调用方）

### Bug 2：交付执行页“操作”按钮点了没反应
#### 根因（已定位）
文件：`pages/admin/fulfillment-run/index.js`  
函数：`onOrderAction(e)`

当前写法等价于：
```js
const idx = Number(dataset.idx || -1)
```
当 `dataset.idx = 0`（第一条订单）时：
- `0 || -1 => -1`
- 触发 `idx < 0` 返回
- 所以第一条订单点“操作”无响应

#### 修复策略（决定）
用“是否存在字段”的方式读取，而不是 `||`：
```js
const rawIdx = e.currentTarget.dataset ? e.currentTarget.dataset.idx : undefined
const idx = rawIdx === undefined ? -1 : Number(rawIdx)
```
或等价写法（关键点：不能把 `0` 当 false）。

### 同类 Bug（顺手修复）
#### 交付准备页 `上移/下移`
文件：`pages/admin/fulfillment-prep/index.js`
- `onMoveUp`
- `onMoveDown`

也用了同类写法：
- `Number(dataset.idx || -1)`

同样会让 `index=0` 的读取异常（尤其“下移第一条”会无响应）。
本次一并修复，避免你下一步再撞一次。

      can-cancel-order="{{canCancelOrder}}"

      bindqtychange="onQtyChange"
      bindremoveitem="onRemoveItem"
      bindsave="onSaveItems"
      bindcancelorder="onCancelOrder"
    />
  </view>
</scroll-view>

+const PAYMENT_METHOD_OPTIONS = [

+
